requirementsVerbatim: Route choice made on concrete info: goal, boss/danger, expected trophy/material/item family, depth, branch consequence, extraction/return condition.

classificationLegend.AVAILABLE: A concrete value or rule for this decision field is emitted on the current wire/source/test surface and can be cited.
classificationLegend.DERIVABLE-WITHOUT-GAMEPLAY-RULES: Not directly emitted as this decision field, but computable purely from cited existing payloads/rules without inventing any campaign, loot, economy, balance, or risk value.
classificationLegend.MISSING: No current source, payload, or test provides the information; producing it would require an owner-only decision.

parityObservations.observation: C++ chart rows omit levelHint and childIds, which the browser chart rows carry (levelHint rendered by Chart.vue); browser chart payload additionally includes houseName.
parityObservations.impact: A native Gate C decider lacks the difficulty band and sibling links unless parity is closed.

parityObservations.observation: Node identity is intentionally not cross-server stable: C++ documents 'The hash need not match JS bit-for-bit' and uses FNV-1a with direct bit slices, while the browser uses xmur3 + mulberry32; name pools also differ (C++ 6x6 compounds, no standalones; JS 12x10 plus 6 standalones with dedup fallback).
parityObservations.impact: The same nodeId string resolves to different name/template/layout/branching per server implementation, so concrete route info captured from the browser reference will not describe the native journey until reconciled or re-derived natively.

parityObservations.observation: Copper Road differs materially: browser pairs are volcanic/sand with the full verdigris blurb; C++ pairs are crypt/wilds with truncated blurbs on every road.
parityObservations.impact: Terroir-driven danger expectations diverge between surfaces.

parityObservations.observation: Browser server pushes world:chart:updated on Warden death; the C++ server emits no such event (clients must re-request world:road:chart).
parityObservations.impact: Native chart freshness behavior differs; harmless for the audit but part of the chart surface.

parityObservations.observation: No chart pane exists in the native client (rg 'chart' over native/client/ returns no matches).
parityObservations.impact: Gate C's deciding surface (chart presentation) is client-pending on native, matching the matrix's server-ready/client-pending pattern.
